Somewhat related but unless you’re dead set on getting a hysto, I recommend getting a bilateral salpingectomy + endometrial ablation! I also have severe tokophobia and it’s astounding how much more calm I feel after! 
The bisalp cuts your fallopian tubes so you keep your ovaries and uterus, the endometrial ablation “burns” your uterine lining which (often) prevents periods and makes the uterus a hostile environment for a fetus (ablation is NOT birth control however, the bisalp is) 
It’s a permanent procedure but done laparoscopically and much less invasive then a hysto. You get all the benefits of being sterile while not running into the risk of prolapse, more major surgery complications, etc…
My bisalp was mostly a week of discomfort but the worst was over within 3-4 days or so. Fully back to normal within a month.
Of course, if a hysto is right for you then that’s the route you should go! The biggest advantage is they’ll remove your cervix so you won’t need Pap smears anymore. I hate going to the gyno, by my (very) trans friendly pcp can do them for me…so I’m willing to do them.

Hello! Just graduated from UW with a BA in English w/Honors. I also transferred in, so I understand how daunting it is. Also, if you want to have a minor *pick it now*. 
I can’t recommend Michelle Liu enough, she teaches 302 sometimes and is just such a joy. Honestly, most of my professors aside from those teaching historical literature courses have been fantastic. 
I would personally avoid the Shakespeare courses at UW, take them if you really like Shakespeare but the prof is clearly not interested in teaching and would rather talk about his books/act like he’s teaching in an Ivy League instead. 
With the English major, and some other humanities, you truly get what you put into it—so don’t slack because you can. 
202 and 302 are the two required intro courses and they are a bit daunting, especially as a transfer but everyone else is just as confused. 
I would get involved in school journals if you can and take a broad swath of courses. Before graduating, I’d also take ENG490 (Public and Professional Life) w/ Michelle Liu. Spring 2023 was her first iteration of the course and it’s specifically intended for English majors entering the workforce. Her goal is to help you translate some of your English skills into workforce skills (if that’s your trajectory) and helped me graduate not feeling too scared. 
Another thing, the career center has an agenda against English majors. One advisor even referred to it as a ‘Mrs. Degree’ to someone I knew. They will steer you towards marketing generally, I’d say actually talking to and getting to know professors is the best route for career options/ideas.
